propositions: The flat per-context character bound (100,000 chars) in _MAX_CONTEXT_CHARS conflates physical capacity (model window fit) with economic cost (recovery fan-out multiplier), causing legitimate contexts like c9f7 (121,147 chars) to be refused at preflight despite fitting within the ratified worst-case product (32 criteria × 100k = 3.2M chars).

The physical ceiling must derive from the resolved verifier model's own context window (not escalation max), moving MODEL_LADDER from plan_review/sizing.py to model_classes.py and adding an own-window accessor that returns 2 × model_window_tokens as the admission limit.

The economic ceiling must be expressed as a product bound _MAX_RECOVERY_INPUT_CHARS = 3,200,000 (context_chars × criteria_count), refusing when the product exceeds it before any runner calls are made.

An append-only comment store with no delete capability means a flat bound can never be raised enough to catch future outliers; the solution must decouple the per-context ceiling from the product bound so either can be tuned independently.

The two-ceiling refusal must remain elision-free and visible with full diagnostics (context_chars, context_char_limit, criteria_total, recovery_input_chars, recovery_input_char_limit), and must preserve d59e's invariants: byte-identical context delivery, criteria budget ≤ context budget, and zero billable calls on over-budget rejection.
